newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair shrugs off talk of Labour landslide.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair shrugs off talk of Labour landslide.

text.p: British opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair on Monday shrugged off suggestions in opinion polls that his party was headed for a landslide victory in the May 1 election.

"I take absolutely nothing for granted in this election at all. We are out over the next few days fighting for every vote. All this talk of landslide -- I don't think there is talk of landslides out there in the country," Blair told BBC radio in an interview
Five opinion polls in the past few days have put Labour's lead over the ruling Conservatives at between 15 and 24 points, which could translate into a 200 seat parliamentary majority for Labour.
But Labour, out of power since 1979, is anxious to avoid complacency.

"I think it is a question now of every single part of the country understanding the simple and stark choice; You can have the same old Conservatives back or you can have a new and revitalised Labour Party," Blair said.
